module_title: Slowdown, Recession, Depression, and Shapes of Recovery
introduction: In the news, the terms Slowdown, Recession, and Depression are often used interchangeably, but in macroeconomics, their definitions are strictly distinct. At this level, we will differentiate these terms and understand the graphical 'Shapes' of an economic recovery.

core_concepts.title: Economic Slowdown
core_concepts.description: A slowdown does NOT mean the GDP is shrinking. It means the GDP is 'still growing, but at a slower pace'. (Example: If India's growth rate drops from 8% to 5%, the GDP is still technically getting larger, but it is experiencing a slowdown).

core_concepts.title: Recession
core_concepts.description: In a recession, the GDP actually shrinks (Negative Growth). The size of the economy becomes smaller than it was in the previous year. (Example: A growth rate of -2%).

core_concepts.title: Depression
core_concepts.description: This is the most severe and destructive form of a contraction. A recession becomes a depression when the economic decline lasts for an unusually long time (years) and the GDP drops by more than 10%. (Example: The Great Depression of 1929).

core_concepts.title: Shapes of Recovery
core_concepts.description: 1. V-shaped: A sharp economic decline followed by a very rapid, strong recovery. 2. U-shaped: A decline, followed by a period of stagnation at the bottom, and then a gradual rise. 3. W-shaped (Double-dip): The economy recovers quickly but falls into a second recession before a full recovery. 4. L-shaped: A severe drop followed by a very long period of flat, stagnant non-growth.

important_entities.title: K-shaped Recovery
important_entities.significance: Highly relevant post-COVID-19. A K-shaped recovery means different parts of the economy recover at entirely different rates. The wealthy and tech sectors recover rapidly (the upward arm of the 'K'), while small businesses and low-income workers continue to suffer and decline (the downward arm of the 'K'), leading to massive wealth inequality.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Assertion-Reasoning questions: If a country's growth rate goes from 7% in Q1 to 4% in Q2, the production has NOT decreased. Production is still increasing, just slower. Do not label this a contraction/recession; it is purely a 'Slowdown'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A Slowdown is the mildest, a Recession is severe, and a Depression is catastrophic.

exam_strategy_tips: State PCS exams frequently ask for the trigger year of the Great Depression. It started with the Wall Street stock market crash in the USA in '1929'.
